Steep
stēp
adj. and n. (sharply sloping; a precipice; rendering Greek kremnos, Hebrew morad and madregah)
Old English stēap, high, lofty. The Gospels' steep place is a cliff over water; the swine went down it.

Biblical Definition

The Gadarene swine: “the whole herd of swine ran violently down a steep place into the sea, and perished in the waters” (Mat 8:32); “the herd ran violently down a steep place into the sea, (they were about two thousand;) and were choked in the sea” (Mar 5:13; Luk 8:33). Micah: the mountains shall be molten “as wax before the fire, and as the waters that are poured down a steep place” (Mic 1:4). At Gog's fall “the mountains shall be thrown down, and the steep places shall fall” (Eze 38:20).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines steep as making a large angle with the plane of the horizon; ascending or descending with great inclination; precipitous; and, as a noun, a precipice.

expand to see more

STEEP, a. Making a large angle with the plane of the horizon; ascending or descending with great inclination; precipitous; as a steep hill or mountain.

STEEP, n. A precipice; a steep ascent or descent.

Key Scripture

Mat 8:32 — "And he said unto them, Go. And when they were come out, they went into the herd of swine: and, behold, the whole herd of swine ran violently down a steep place into the sea, and perished in the waters."

Mar 5:13 — "And forthwith Jesus gave them leave. And the unclean spirits went out, and entered into the swine: and the herd ran violently down a steep place into the sea, (they were about two thousand;) and were choked in the sea."

Luk 8:33 — "Then went the devils out of the man, and entered into the swine: and the herd ran violently down a steep place into the lake, and were choked."

Mic 1:4 — "And the mountains shall be molten under him, and the valleys shall be cleft, as wax before the fire, and as the waters that are poured down a steep place."

Eze 38:20 — "So that the fishes of the sea, and the fowls of the heaven, and the beasts of the field, and all creeping things that creep upon the earth, and all the men that are upon the face of the earth, shall shake at my presence, and the mountains shall be thrown down, and the steep places shall fall, and every wall shall fall to the ground."

Modern Corruption

The town asked Jesus to leave over the price of the swine, and the modern reader is on the town's side without knowing it.

expand to see more

The devils asked to go into the swine, the Lord gave them leave, and two thousand pigs went down a steep place into the sea. The demons' destination is always a steep place and a sea; permission to enter a lower host is the only mercy they get, and it ends in the water. The town's response is the part the reader should notice: they came out, saw the man clothed and in his right mind, and besought Jesus to depart out of their coasts, because the swine had been worth more to them than the neighbour. Every generation has its own two thousand swine, the economy it would rather keep than see a man delivered at its cost, and the modern objector who calls the miracle wasteful has joined the delegation that asked Him to leave. Micah's steep place is the other picture: the mountains poured down like water when the LORD comes out of His place — nothing high stays high before Him.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Greek kremnos (G2911), a precipice, steep place; Hebrew morad (H4174), a descent, slope; madregah (H4095), a steep place, cliff.

expand to see more

Greek kremnos (G2911) — a precipice; Matthew 8:32, Mark 5:13, Luke 8:33.

Hebrew morad (H4174) — a descent, steep place; Micah 1:4, Joshua 7:5; madregah (H4095), Ezekiel 38:20, Song of Solomon 2:14.

Usage

"“Ran violently down a steep place into the sea” — the demons' destination."

"“They were about two thousand” — the price of a delivered man, and the town's answer."

"“As the waters that are poured down a steep place” — the mountains before the LORD."
